items.label: 6. How to Verify the Contract On-Chain

abstract.title: 1. Abstract
abstract.p1: Polnation is an Agentic AI Earning platform deployed on Polygon PoS. The product uses an off-chain agentic earning engine to read public USDC balance data, apply balance-tier and risk rules, and surface daily earning eligibility without requiring users to deposit funds into Polnation custody.
abstract.p2: The technical thesis is simple: the AI/agent layer can compute, rank, and automate earning logic, but the trust boundary must remain public and auditable. That boundary is the verified Polnation MerkleTree contract on PolygonScan.
bullets: Agentic earning engine reads public on-chain state, balance tiers, user eligibility, and operational guardrails before producing earning actions.
The Polygon contract 0x6c4C745d909B13528e638C7Aa63ABA9406fA8c63 is listed on PolygonScan as Source Code Verified / Exact Match with contract name PolnationMerkleTree.
PolygonScan surfaces the Polnation: Merkle Tree label context, giving users a public identity reference instead of an opaque contract address.
Polnation does not require an unlimited standing USDC approval. Where a permit-based flow is used, the user signs a specific authorization and the resulting action is visible on-chain.
Users can inspect the verified Solidity source, ABI, owner, USDC address, and emitted events directly on PolygonScan.
abstract.proof: Polnation is not asking users to trust a hidden black-box contract. The MerkleTree contract is public, verified on PolygonScan, labeled in the Polnation context, and independently inspectable by any wallet user, auditor, or exchange risk engine.

architecture.title: 2. System Architecture
architecture.p1: The Polnation system consists of three independent layers that interact through well-defined interfaces.
principles: Separation of concerns: the computation layer never holds private keys to user wallets. It only reads public on-chain data and publishes verifiable outputs.
Trustless verification: contract identity, source code, ABI, and events can be checked by any independent observer.
No single point of custody: user funds remain on the USDC contract and any token movement must be explicitly authorized by the user through a verified contract boundary.

auth.title: 3. Non-Custodial & Scoped Authorization Model
auth.p1: The most critical security property of Polnation is its non-custodial, scoped-authorization architecture. It avoids unlimited standing approvals and separates off-chain earning logic from on-chain execution.
auth.risk: Any contract with a non-zero approval can call transferFrom on approved tokens. Malicious or compromised contracts with unlimited approvals can drain wallets, which is why scoped authorization matters.
auth.proof: Users can check USDC allowance on-chain and inspect the verified PolnationMerkleTree source at

audit.title: 4. How to Verify: Authorization & Approval Audit Guide
audit.p1: Do not trust the UI alone. Users can independently check approvals and inspect the verified contract boundary.
polygonscanSteps: Open polygonscan.com and search your wallet address.
Open Token Approvals and filter for USDC on Polygon.
Verify that no unexpected or unlimited Polnation-related approval is present.
Open the PolnationMerkleTree contract page and confirm Source Code Verified / Exact Match.
revokeSteps: Enter your wallet address or connect your wallet.
Revoke stale or unfamiliar approvals directly from the tool.

contract.title: 5. Verified MerkleTree Contract on PolygonScan
contract.p1: The primary technical proof for Polnation Agentic AI Earning is the public contract record on PolygonScan. The MerkleTree contract is source-code verified, exposes a readable ABI, and carries Polnation Merkle Tree identity context on the explorer.
why: Exact Match means the deployed bytecode corresponds to the published Solidity source.
Wallets and auditors can inspect functions such as executeWithPermit, getAllowance, owner, usdc, name, and version.
Permit execution emits PermitExecuted(owner, recipient, amount, operationId), allowing actions to be correlated on-chain.
The Polnation Merkle Tree label context makes the explorer record easier to distinguish from phishing or cloned contracts.
Verification proves inspectability; it does not remove all smart-contract, owner-key, or business-process risk.

verify.title: 6. How to Verify the Contract On-Chain
verify.p1: Users do not need to trust Polnation marketing copy. The contract can be verified directly from PolygonScan.
steps: Open the PolnationMerkleTree contract on PolygonScan.
Confirm the page metadata shows Contract: Verified.
Open the Contract tab and confirm Source Code Verified with Exact Match.
Inspect src/PolnationMerkleTree.sol and the ABI functions exposed by PolygonScan.
For executed permit flows, check Events for PermitExecuted and match owner, recipient, amount, and operationId.
verify.claim: The Agentic AI Earning narrative is backed by a public verification path: a named contract, verified source, readable ABI, and event-level audit trail on PolygonScan.

engine.title: 7. Agentic Earning Architecture
engine.p1: The earning layer is agentic because it continuously evaluates public on-chain state and routes users through the safest available earning path. The AI/agent layer can automate analysis and decisions, but it cannot secretly move funds.
engine.formula: Earning Signal = f(USDC Balance Tier, Eligibility Rules, Referral Momentum, Pool Budget, Risk Guardrails)
proves: The contract users interact with is not an anonymous bytecode blob.
Wallets and auditors can inspect which functions may move USDC and under what permissions.
The contract name, source, ABI, and event definitions can be checked independently of the frontend.
The Agentic AI layer remains off-chain; the on-chain boundary remains deterministic and inspectable.

risk.title: 8. Compliance & Risk Framework
disclosures: Smart contracts carry inherent risk even when source code is verified.
Returns depend on operational performance, ecosystem conditions, and platform growth; they are not guaranteed.
USDC is a centralized stablecoin managed by Circle; depeg or issuer risk affects all USDC holders.
Polygon network congestion or validator issues may delay actions.
Regulatory changes may affect platform operations in some jurisdictions.
protections: If Polnation ceases operations, users keep their USDC in their own wallets.
Polnation emphasizes no unlimited standing approval and scoped user-approved actions.
Contract identity, source, ABI, and events are publicly visible.
Users can move their USDC at any time with no withdrawal lock from Polnation.
